detectors.name: AP1-raw-rva
detectors.message: Anti-pattern WARN (AP1 raw RVA): adds a hardcoded base+offset literal. RVAs shift per KCD2 update - resolve by Address Library ID instead (author a row in the reference DB via the maintainer tool; the curated CSVs export to data/db-export/, the reference DB regenerates from them - .claude/rules/address-library.md). Bypass: '// approved: <reason>' on the line after user sign-off.

detectors.name: AP4-hook-outside-engine
detectors.message: Anti-pattern WARN (AP4 hook outside the engine): calls MinHook directly. Production hooks register a conflict_engine footprint and apply via g_applyOrder - they don't call MH_* directly (.claude/rules/hook-engine.md). Bypass: '// approved: <reason>' after user sign-off.

detectors.name: AP4-applyall-in-production
detectors.message: Anti-pattern WARN (AP4 ApplyAll in production): adds an ApplyAll() call. Production orchestration walks conflict_engine::g_applyOrder (priority asc, name asc); ApplyAll() reintroduces the patches-always-before-hooks ordering bug (.claude/rules/hook-engine.md). Bypass: '// approved: <reason>' after user sign-off.

detectors.name: AP5-lua-sentinel
detectors.message: Anti-pattern WARN (AP5 Lua sentinel): adds a `static const Node/TValue`. Its address ends up in a GCObject on g->rootgc and trips WHGame's GC -> STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION (.claude/rules/lua-bridge.md). Use raw Lua C API / registry refs / userdata. Bypass: '// approved: <reason>' after user sign-off.

detectors.name: AP7-test-absence
detectors.message: Anti-pattern WARN (AP7 test coverage): this is engine code. New capability or observable behavior change -> a test-plugins/ regression plugin ships in the SAME unit of work (build it now, don't wait to be asked). A behavior-changing bug fix -> a sub-test in that feature's existing plugin reproducing the bug. Pure internal refactor with no observable change -> no new test needed; say so. Per .claude/rules/test-suite.md (AP7).
